The game's file is this recording played twice and a bit, summed at the joins, not cut. The recording's own ending restates its opening exactly one period later (82.9267s; self-correlation 0.93), and the game reads it at three lags: pass 1 at +1.215634s from the start; pass 2 at -81.711033s, faded in under pass 1's natural ending from 83.4s and full by about 89s (pass 1 keeps playing its own ending at full level until it dies at 93s); and from 165.86s the file's own head copied at one loop length (lag -164.64033s), which is what makes the loop wrap continuous, with pass 2's ending carrying on under it for about 2s. Pass 2 also sits about 1.2 dB above pass 1 as it enters, settling to -0.4 dB by the loop end. The old item cut to pass 2 at 91.1s, after pass 1 had run out, with both offsets 4-19 ms off. Rebuilt as ONE segment: the recording at +1.215634s, summed with itself delayed by 7960960 samples at 96 kHz (pass 2, through a piecewise gain that follows the measured fade-in and level), by 15922170 samples (the head copy; equal to the loop length, so the wrap is sample-continuous) and by 7961210 samples from 165.84s (pass 2's ending, fading out from 166.6s over 1.2s). Against the game's own file: weighted 0.9599 -> 0.9945, envelope hole 35.9 dB at 90.5s -> 0.9 dB, tail 0.906 -> 0.991 against a control of 0.995, no joins left (was: outgoing runs out before the join at 91.1s). The exact offsets alone gave 0.9944 but kept the 36 dB hole. Level: apply's gain is peak-limited to +0.7 dB (matched +2.1 dB) because the game's file peaks at +0.9 dBFS, so the whole build sits about 0.8 dB under the game; raising pass 3's own +0.7 dB lowers the limit by the same amount, so it is left at unity.
